feedback: The increased sensor count to 7 and larger sensor size improved line detection resolution and sensitivity, as intended. The wider wheel track at 0.15 likely helped turning stability somewhat. However, the robot still went off track on both development tracks without line loss events, indicating the controller struggled with steering precision and stability in curves. The moderate steering oscillation and off-track terminations suggest the controller had to compensate for insufficient control responsiveness and possible overshoot. The base speed of 0.12 was likely too high for the current geometry and controller, limiting control precision in curves. The sensor weights from -1.0 to 1.0 are appropriate for 7 sensors, but the controller gains need tuning to balance responsiveness and stability.
requested_changes: controller.kp to 1.0 to increase proportional control and improve steering precision
controller.kd to 0.015 to reduce overshoot and steering oscillation
controller.ki to 0.06 to better correct steady-state errors
controller.base_speed to 0.11 to allow more precise control in curves
